properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/28/2021 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Monroe Twp, Bradford county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/27/2021
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 940412
Permit API: 015-22501
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Monroe Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/28/2021
Comments: Eric Hottenstein (Chesapeake) notified Carrie Knapp (NCRO) that at 1530 hrs Monday December 27, 2021 they discovered approximately 112 barrels of produced water/freshwater spilled. A flowback tank in containment leaked, and the containment leaked onto the pad. (CTS 361265). I spoke with William Dolan (Creston Environmental LLC) on site. He explained they are using a YSI meter and a soil probe to delineate the extent of the reported 112 barrel brine/freshwater mix release to the pad surface which occurred yesterday. A vac truck with a T adapter (photo) is removing that liquid from the pad surface. A track hoe (photo) is removing the impacted pad soil/rock and loading into a dump-truck. The truck then dumps the material on liner containment (photo) on the opposite side of the pad. I used an Oakton PCSTestr 35 to get electrical conductivity (EC) readings from pooled liquid on the pad surface. In the area where the release occurred, it gave readings of 8.0-12.2 mS/cm. I collected liquid sample 0935-429 from the area that was 12.2 mS/cm. Pooled liquid on the pad surface unaffected by the release is 0.16-0.22 mS/cm. I also used a Hanna soil probe to get EC readings from the pad material. In the excavated area it gave a 0.04 mS/cm reading; the unexcavated area immediately outside it gave readings of 3.0-4.0 mS/cm. 4.0 mS /cm is the max limit for the Hanna soil probe. The EC readings indicate the brine release did not flow outside of the pad surface. Rock, vegetation, and straw mulch stabilize soil of the site. I did not observe accelerated erosion or sedimentation. Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Cleanup of this spill will be referred to the DEP ECB program for Act 2 compliance. Air temp 40F JLP

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 965072
Permit API: 125-28223
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/12/2022
Comments: On August 12 2022, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill release reported by the Operator to the Department on 8/12/2022 for the Huffys Family Unit 16H OG Well. The Department was accompanied by Derek Zofchak(Range Resources) and Chase Kolence(Range Resources). The findings were as follows:Per Mr. Zofchak, produced water was released due to a corrisive elbow on production equipment(see photo 9). It was estimated that approximately 10 gallons of produced water was released onto the ground next to the 16H GPU. The 16H GPU failed to be in secondary containment. The Operator has entered into a COA on October 7, 2020 with the Department to install this GPU in secondary containment; therefore, this specific finding of today's inspection is ICS. At the time of the inspection, Act 9 sign was installed at access road. ERP plans were present on site in mailbox. Clean up was currently being conducted with a jack hammer to loosen the affected gravel and then being sucked into a HiVac, into a roll-off box(see photo 6). Excess production fluid, on the ground was absorbed by absorbing pads(see photos 5,7,and 9). Conductivity readings were 5.67mS (release site) and 0.08mS(background reading). The Department request that the Operator submit waste manifests once available. The Department will conduct follow up inspection to verify all impacted material has been removed. Based on today's observations violations will be issued under (78a54, 78a57a, 91.34a and SWMA 301).

Permit API: 033-23623
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Bell Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/09/2023
Comments: Routine site inspection at conventional well 033-23623 on May 9, 2023. Flakey paint and corrosion was observed on the production equipment and axillary pipes. The Department recommends monitoring the equipment and repainting or replacing the equipment if needed. A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were detected.Exposed soil and dead vegetation was observed downslope of the production equipment. The exposed soil was inundated with deer tracks. I screened the area for conductivity using a Hanna soil probe. Elevated soil readings were observed ranging from 1.0 mS/cm to 3.75 mS/cm. I collected a soil sample (3442-664). The sample was sent to the Departments lab in Harrisburg and will be analyzed for SAC 530 plus, bromide, lithium, and strontium. The Department recommends that the operator address the remediation of the brine release in accordance with small spill policy 800-5000-001. Violations have been cited.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-10-30 to Ard Opr Llc in Grugan Twp, Clinton county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Ard Opr Llc

Violation Date: 2019-10-30
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 866619
Permit API: 035-21253
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-10-30
Comments: On October 30, 2019 , DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a spill investigation (CTS # 346141) at Alta Operating LLC. COP Tract 285 Pad G. The spill was reported at 0935 that a plug in the dump line of one of the GPUs was not replaced after maintenance on the line was completed. This caused a spill of about 1.9 bbls into the secondary containment and the pad surface. The DEP met with Alta staff Rick Hall and Mark Barbier, they estimated that about a 1 bbl was spilled outside of containment. During the investigation, there was a vacuum tank onsite dewatering the secondary containment of the GPUs. There is a ground wire in the area of the spill, so they were awaiting staff to locate the wire before excavation of the impacted soil could begin. The area of impact is approximately 10'x60'. Water in the secondary containment was screened for conductivity and returned a reading of 1070 uS/cm. A puddle of water in the impacted area was screened and returned a conductivity reading of 5,500 uS/cm. One 25 yard rollback dumpster was onsite to dispose of the impacted soil. The release of production fluid outside of secondary containment is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Section 301 of the Solid Waste Management Act and §78a.54. Due to the volume of the production fluid spilled outside of containment, characterization of the extent of the pollution in accordance of §78a.66(c). The DEP recommends proceeding in accordance with Act 2 remediation.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 10/22/2025 to EQT PROD CO in West Deer Township, Allegheny county. 78a55(h) - EMERGNCY RESPONSE – Emergency Contacts –Operator’s PPC plan failed to contain a list of emergency contact phone numbers for the area in which the well site is located.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a55(h) - EMERGNCY RESPONSE – Emergency Contacts –Operator’s PPC plan failed to contain a list of emergency contact phone numbers for the area in which the well site is located.
Violation ID: 8253262
Permit API: 003-22693
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: West Deer Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/22/2025
Comments: On October 22 2025, the Department conducted a complaint inspection at the Leto Well Pad in regards to CTS 393117. (Erosion and Sediment (E and S) Permit (ESP07022400100E) was issued by the Department for this site on 9/24/2024 and expires on 9/23/2029). Present during the inspection was operator representative Steven Mackey.At the time of the inspection, the Act 9 sign was posted at the access road entrance and appeared to be installed and fabricated in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), and the Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan (PPC) were located within the on-site mailbox. The access road appeared to stabilized with gravel.At the time of the inspection, drilling of the 5H well was ongoing. It appeared secondary containment has been installed, and all required materials and equipment were placed with in the secondary containment. The Department did not observe any holes or active leaks onto the ground from the secondary containments.While onsite, the Department inquired to Mr. Mackey if there had been any recent spills or releases on the well site. Mr. Mackey stated that there was a spill on October 1 2025. He stated the spill was approximately 1.5 gallons of synthetic base oil. He stated the spill occurred from a pin hole in a hose causing the synthetic base oil to spill outside of secondary containment onto the well pad gravel. He stated the spill was immediately remediated and all impacted material removed from the well site. The Department inspected the area of the alleged spill and did not observe any staining or visually impacted gravel. The Department was unable to obtain conductivity readings due to the gravel being heavily compacted. It appeared the spill was visually remediated in accordance with the Department's Spill Policy.Mr. Mackey provided the Department the SDS sheet for this synthetic base oil upon request. The Department also requested the well sites secondary containment logs. Mr. Mackey stated he was unsure of how to access them as they were in their online database. However, the Department spoke to operator representative Jared Lowry via phone call who was able to provide them in an email prior to leaving the site. Mr. Lowry's emails are attached to this inspection report.Prior to leaving the site, the Department reviewed the Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan with in the onsite mailbox. Upon review, the Department did not observe the spill described above listed in the Pollution History section of the PPC. As noted in Guidelines for the Development and Implementation of Environmental Emergency Response Plans, # 400-2200-001: The operator shall list the previous pollution incidents, the date, the material or waste spilled, approximate amount spilled, environmental damage, and action taken to prevent a recurrence. The Department recommends the operator update the onsite PPC as necessary to ensure it contains all required information.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to have the PPC properly updated. Although the citation is listed as 78a55(h), 78a55(g) is being cited. Due to an app error, 78a55(g) is not able to be selected as a citation.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-01-10 to Chevron Appalachia Llc in South Huntingdon Twp, Westmoreland county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Chevron Appalachia Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-01-10
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 873919
Permit API: 129-28979
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: South Huntingdon Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2020-01-10
Comments: As documented in Inspection Record #2971125, the self-reported amount of oil-based mud released was 5 barrels (see Spill/Release Information of Photo #2). The Department recommended remediating the spill pursuant to §78a66(c)2 in an Inspection received by the operator on December 13, 2019. As of January 10, 2019, a satisfactory initial written report pursuant to §78a66(c)2 has not been received. The report provided by the operator on December 12, 2019 and documented in Inspection Record #2971125 only satisfies §78a66(c)2(i)(A), (C), and (F). Inspection Records #2970703 and #2971139 shows petroleum-based mud in multiple locations on the pad. Inspection Record #2971139 shows an unknown substance with a rainbow sheen discharging from under secondary containment at least 100 feet from the well heads. The Department collected multiple sample on the site on December 6, 2019. Sample results show the petroleum-based mud in an erosion rill greater than 200 feet from the well heads. The rill is on the edge of the well pad and discharges toward a stormwater channel which leads to the PCSM forebay; this evidence is sufficient to not only show the extent of the spill, but also that the spilled material has left the well pad and entered stormwater facilities. Per a telephone conversation with Chevron representative B. A. Lambie on January 8, 2020, the initial remediation by Chevron was completed on December 9, 2019. Department personnel were on-site on December 9, 2019 as documented in Inspection Record #298131. At the time of inspection, secondary containment was still in place. A strong petroleum odor and non-bacterial sheen were observed near and in stormwater channel R-4, respectively. The Department collected multiple samples from the site on December 27, 2019. The rill and nearby areas had not been altered as of December 27, 2019, nor had channel R-4. Sample results from December 27, 2019 show hexane is present in at least three locations in the material spilled near the pad entrance as mentioned in Inspection Record #2970703. The spilled material will need remediated pursuant to §78a66(c). At this time, hexane is being treated as a separate spill. Additional violations are being issued. Photographs are referenced as part of the operator-provided inspections provided on December 16, 2019 as requested in Inspection Record #2971139. However, the photographs cannot be accessed. Therefore, the inspections provided were incomplete. The photographs were requested via e-mail on December 17, 2019. As of January 10, 2019, the photographs have not been provided. Additional violations may be forthcoming based on review of the complete inspections. In Inspection Record #2971139, the Department requested photographic documentation of the removal of the secondary containment that remained on December 6, 2019 be provided by December 27, 2019. As of January 10, 2019, the documentation has not been provided.

Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 6/17/2021
Comments: This admin inspection is in response to the receipt of partial analytical results for sample number 0718-177, taken on 6/7/21 as part of inspection number 3202448 on Pad B. Elevated strontium and aluminum in the analytical results indicate the release of a pollutional substance. In a call on 6/10/21 between Sean Vanfleet, DEP WQSS, and Rick Hall, representative for ARD, Mr. Hall said that there had previously been a tank containing brine on Pad B while the drilling operation was rigging up. He stated he found out from site personnel that the tank had leaked and released an estimated 20 barrels of brine onto secondary containment. Mr. Hall said that the berms on the secondary containment were not fully installed at that time and the fluid ran toward the area of the pad surface where sample 0718-177 was taken. Mr. Hall said that Creston Environmental screened the pad and found elevated conductivity in the travel lane where sample 0718-177 was taken. He said that the pad surface was scraped down to a depth of approximately 1" in this area. He said 3 boxes were filled with the excavated material. He stated that fluid with an elevated conductivity continued to seep out from beneath the secondary containment so a sump has been installed to collect this fluid. The remainder of the pad was also screened by Creston according to Rick. Creston also took a sample from the same area where sample 0718-177 was taken. Mr. Hall said that the company man did not initially report the release from the tank as he believed that the fluid had stayed on the secondary containment. Based on the estimated release volume, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. Violations noted. Outstanding violations noted.

Comments: On February 4, 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Aphrodite Well Site (ESCGP issued on 5/9/2020, amended on 2/5/2024, expiring on 2/4/2029) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 2/3/2026 (CTS 394941). Present during the inspection was operator representative Jim Noon.According to Mr.Noon, this release is a seperate release, unrelated to the release documented in inspection report 4125373.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel.At the time of inspection, there are 5 total wells on the well pad. According to the operator, stimulation for all 5 wells has been completed and they are continuing to install production equipment in order to get the wells into active production.During the inspection, Mr. Noon guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Noon the release was discovered on 2/3/2026 when containment for drilling/stimulation equipment was being removed from the site. He stated that upon removal of the containment, staining was observed and after further assessment it was identified as a release of impaired water and reported to the Department. At the time of the inspection the operator is unsure of the total volume of impaired water that was released.The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the release and ongoing remediation was in an approximate 40-foot by 80-foot area adjacent to the well heads near the entrance of the well pad.Mr. Noon stated that 2 small temporary sumps were excavated in the area of the release in order to isolate the release. The water collected in the sumps were being pumped out by a vacuum truck. Mr. Noon stated that 2 roll-off boxes had already been filled with impacted material, and they were waiting for additional boxes to continue remediation.Conductivity readings of 18.08mS, and 6.13mS were obtained in the 2 excavated sumps. Conductivity readings of 3.97mS, 1.25mS, 1.17mS, and 0.69mS were obtained in the area of the release/remediation.The Department requests the operator provide a copy of the secondary containment inspection records from January 1, 2026, through the date the secondary containment was removed, within 3 days of receiving this inspection report.The operator is also requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.If the quantity of the spill is determined to be greater than 1 barrel (42 gallons),the operator will need to perform remediation in accordance with the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2).Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued against the Aphrodite 2M well for the observed release. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt and review of the requested information/documentation.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/26/2024
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a release of produced fluid that occurred on 12/25/24. I spoke with Mike Demming (CHK) during the inspection. The release occurred due to produced fluid freezing in a pipe on a filter pot. The burst pipe allowed the produced fluid to spray onto the pad and into the production tank secondary containment.The impacted area of the pad was estimated to be 80' by 12'. The volume of fluid released was estimated to be between 1.5 and 2 barrels based on the fluid levels in the affected equipment. Conductivity readings were taken by CHK both on the pad surface and directly from the broken pipe. The conductivity readings were at or below 1 milliesiemen per centimeter (mS/cm). There was some black material that was released with the produced fluid.The pad surface was covered by snow and ice and did not appeared to be directly impacted. The impacted snow and frozen produced fluid were removed and placed into the production tank secondary containment. Comments: On 5/8/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident inspection at the Repsol Alderson V 05-009 well site. This was in response to a spill notification of five gallons of antifreeze that the department received from Repsol on 5/6/2023.Prior to arrival at the site, I contacted JD Ressler of Repsol, the person who had submitted the notification of the spill to the department. JD said that at approximately 2:30 AM on 5/6/2023, a truck driver drove over a concrete barricade, dragging the barricade along under his truck for a distance on the pad surface. The concrete barricade did damage an antifreeze line on the truck, releasing approximately 5 gallons of antifreeze to the pad surface. Upon discovery, the leak was stopped and oil soaks were placed on the pad surface to absorb the fluid. The contaminated oil soaks were placed into trash bags. This waste material was brought to the Warner 05121 well site in Susquehanna county where fracking operations are currently being conducted. The waste material will be disposed by Environmental Resources out of Tunkhannock, PA.It was 55 degrees and partly cloudy when I arrived on location. Repsol is using the Alderson V 009 location to stage trucks that are servicing a nearby frac site in Susquehanna County. Sand and water trucks were on location, driving in and out during the inspection. At the site, I met with Repsol's Andrew Senefelder. Andrew led me to the location of the spill. Andrew said that the truck driver did run over and drag one concrete block, and also drug another concrete block that was attached via a cable. These concrete blocks are approximately 2' x 2' x 8' and can be viewed in pictures 3 and 4. I did look around the area described as where the spill took place. I screened water puddles in the area for conductivity with results at 0.4 mS conductance or less. I also viewed the puddles and the surface of the ground. I did not witness any discoloration or evidence of contamination in this area. Discussing the location of the waste, Andrew did say that the contaminated material was being brought back to this well site and would be disposed of from this site.Water puddles from recent rainfall were scattered across the pad surface. I field tested these for conductivity with results at 0.4 mS or less. I did not witness the emergency response plan at the entrance to the facility. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by two bio retention basins. Bio retention basin 1 is adequately stabilized and functioning as designed with minimal evidence of standing water. Bio retention basin 2 does have wetland foliage and standing water.There was one well staged for production. The well was tagged with the API/well permit number. No bubbling within the cellar was observed. The GPU and production tank had secondary containment. This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; SWMA 301, CSL 402, and 25 PA Code 78a.56. The spill had been cleaned up, resulting in VIOICs (Violation noted and Immediately Corrected).The DEP recommends the following: 1. Screen the area impacted by the release of antifreeze for additional contamination and continue with cleanup as necessary.2. Assess the stability and functionality of bio retention basin 2 and repair as necessary.3. Place a copy of the site emergency response plan at the entrance to the facility.I left the site at 1330 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: JKLM ENERGY LLC

Violation Date: 7/12/2021
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 922940
Permit API: 105-21875
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Ulysses Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/12/2021
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of JKLM's Headwaters 145 Pad located in Ulysses Township, Potter County on 7/12/2021 at 1040 hours. The weather was 76 degrees with mostly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a reported release of ~42 gallons of production fluid to the pad surface. The release occurred on Saturday, 7/10/2021, and was properly reported to the DEP. Complaint ID #357917 is tied to this release. On 7/10/2021, at approximately 1210 hours, a fitting on a hose line connected to a production line riser failed, causing a reported release of ~42 gallons of production fluid to the pad surface. A vacuum truck was onsite when the release occurred and was able to vacuum up the fluid that was visible. Excavation of the pad material began on Saturday. A rain event on Sunday evening caused pooling of water in the excavated areas, which was again vacuumed up. Environmental consultant, Whipper Hill was onsite during the inspection on Monday, where screening and excavating of the impacted area was being conducted. Whipper Hill reported elevated soil conductivity readings from 3-6mS/cm. I screened the impacted area for soil conductivity with a Hanna Groline soil tester. Some isolated areas were field measured >4.00mS/cm. Standing water along the edge of the pad closest to the release was field measured at ~370us/cm today (see photo #5). The release was contained to the pad surface and no erosion & sediment controls or stormwater controls were affected. The impacted area was still being screened and excavated when I left the site. Based on the findings outlined within this inspection report, violations of the following are cited against API # 105-21875 at this time: 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a) 35 P.S. 6018.301 Due to the volume of the release being reported at ~42 gallons and then a commingling of impacted soils and rainwater after the initial release, this release will be referred to the DEP's Cleanups and Brownfields Program for attainment with Act 2 standards. I departed the site at 1150 hours.

Permit API: 053-27204
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Jenks Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-08-20
Comments: Site of oil release reported on 6/21/2019 was from the secondary containment of a tank battery located east off Salmon Road in a forested area. Oil was released from a hole in the bottom of one of the tanks located in a plastic lined secondary containment. An estimated several barrels of oil were released into the secondary containment. The valved discharge pipe through the secondary containment embankment was open for an unknown period of time after the tank was breached allowing the flow of an estimated one barrel of oil to be released to the ditch north of the tank battery. The oil released into the ditch flowed through a culvert under the access road and continued to spread out and flow through vegetation approximately 400 feet. Moody & Associates has been employed to coordinate the clean-up of this crude oil release. Jordan Sipos, P.G. completed the testing to establish the extent of the release and contaminated soil. Clean-up of the contaminated soil appears to be completed. Soil removal has been extended several hundred feet north of the area originally flagged as showing oil contamination from the release. Four piles of contaminated soil have been secured adjacent to the clean-up area until testing has been completed for disposal. A temporary road has been stoned to access the area and for the eventual removal of the contaminated soil. Manifest for the removal and disposal of the contaminated soil need to be submitted to the Department to lift the violations associated with this release. The removal of the contaminated soil was completed with the least disturbance possible to the surrounding vegetation and without creating a muddy unstable area. Replacement of topsoil and vegetation of this area needs to be coordinated with landowner and State Forest representatives. 15 Day initial Response Letter received July 1, 2019 for Alternate Remediation provision found in the PA DEP Oil and Gas Spill Policy. The report for the clean-up and restoration of the area needs to be submitted to the Department and approved before violations can be lifted.

Both pads and the access road were snow-covered during this inspection. The completions operations have ceased on Pad B and the snubbing rigs and their associated equipment have been removed from the pad. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad B. A representative from Creston Environmental was present on location as well. A crew was working on installing the GPUs on the pad. Trenches were being dug for the flow lines which will run from the well heads to the GPUs on the west side of the pad. A large trench was present at the well heads. Some fluid was seeping into this trench from the fill material surrounding the well cellar for well B-11H. The electrical conductivity (EC) of this fluid was 2.45 mS/cm. A vacuum truck was sucking up this fluid during this inspection. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum up any elevated EC fluid found on the pad surface or during excavation on the pad. The modular aboveground storage structure (MASS) was empty during this inspection. A work crew was beginning to disassemble the MASS during this inspection. The north central area of the well pad has been excavated. One area is a long horizontal area approximately two feet of the north stormwater channel. The EC of the fluid here was 3.35 to 5.41 mS/cm. Another excavated area is to the southwest. According to Mr. Subra, EQT believes that the produced fluid that had been released to this area flowed along an area that had previously been excavated in association with a release that occurred during drilling operations on the well pad. Mr. Subra also said that the northwest area of the well pad where clamshell boxes had led to a release in the dancefloor area has been fully excavated. Additional excavation would still need to occur in the north central area of the well pad as well as in the northeast corner of the pad where the MASS still is present, he also stated. The lined sump remains at the east outlet of the north stormwater channel.Violations remain outstanding for the reported release of produced fluid to the surface of Pad B on permit 081-21880.Violations remain outstanding for the reported release of produced fluid from the MASS from 12/19/22.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a ROUTINE inspection of the Seneca Resources - Gee 832 Well Site located in Middlebury Twp, Tioga Co. on 3/9/21 @0950 hours. The weather was 45 degrees and sunny. No activity or personnel was observed onsite. The site consists of a long access road, well pad and perimeter controls. The majority of the well pad was clear of snow and ice with some piles still melting along the edges. Frozen fluid was observed in the infiltration basin off the corner of the well pad. What appeared to be frost was observed on the production tank onsite. Upon closer inspection, the tank appeared to be covered in crystalized salt originating from the top hatch of the tank . The front 1/3 of the "Highland" production tank and a small ~5'x5' area in front of the tank were observed to have the salt material on it. The pad surface in front of the tank was observed damp. Soil conductivity of the damp area was measured with a Groline soil conductivity probe and found to be >4.0mS/cm directly adjacent to the yellow barrel. Other areas screened within the 5'x5' area in front of the tank were found to have a field measured conductivity of 2.18mS/cm and 1.7mS/cm. Due to the lack of cell phone service onsite, I traveled to a nearby well pad with known cell phone service to contact the operator. I then returned to the well site to complete the inspection. Seneca representative Jake Chambers arrived onsite in response to the release. Mr. Chambers and I discussed the possible causes for the release and the impacted area. Mr. Chambers stated he would immediately mobilize people and equipment to wash down the tank and remove any impacted pad material Jeff Passerrello, Seneca Resources, submitted confirmation of the remediation of the release at the Gee 832 Well Pad via email. Mr. Passerrello stated the release was estimated to have happened between Sunday 3/7/21 and the morning of the DEP inspection. The operator had unloaded the wells to the production tanks on Sunday, which they believe caused a mist of production fluid to coat the tank and gravel. The release was estimated to be approximately 5 gallons. Crews removed the impacted gravel, which was placed into 3 drums. A depth of 3" of material was removed from in front of the tank. The tank was also cleaned with freshwater and scrub brushes. Violations of the following regulations are cited as Immediately Corrected: 25 Pa Code 78a57(a)Control, Storage and disposal of production fluids CSL402(b)Potential Pollution SWMA 301 Management of residual waste I departed the site at 1145 hours.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/15/2023
Comments: This was an inspection performed following a report that the operator had a leaking brine tank on the Enis Lease. I inspected all three tank batteries on this lease.This well is producing and is equipped with a gas powered pumpjack. No spills or leaks are noted at the well. There is a tank battery near the well with two 210 barrel stock tanks contained. There is a buried brine tank across the access road in a wooded area. It appears that there has been an ongoing small leak in the tank, which has allowed brine to leak out into the soil. Impacted soil is apparent ~35 linear feet from the tank, at the base of a small hill. A check with a soil EC meter showed conductivity ranging from 1.5 to 5 mS in the soil. The liquid, along with deer activity, has stripped away vegetation from a 10x15 foot area. The water does not appear to have traveled much further than this and does not appear to be a threat to enter the waters of the Commonwealth.After this visit, I called the operator and he came to the site a little later to look at it with me. He agreed that the tank appeared to be leaking. I suggested that the tank would need to be vacuumed out, removed from the ground and the impacted soils remediated. He said that he would be contacting a contractor immediately to begin this process. Continued followup will be done as necessary.
